title: Painting the shop floor without wrecking your layout
target: How to change the shop floor in Supermarket Simulator using the game's own floor painting behaviour, and what to get out of the way before you start.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop floor you own and can walk on
A floor box available to you
Shelving you are willing to move or work around

steps.do: Get hold of a floor box before you plan the colour, and keep it with you while you paint.
steps.because: the floor is painted from a box you handle rather than from a menu (FloorBox)

steps.do: Move or work around the shelving instead of painting straight through it.
steps.because: the floor is a surface the game repaints, so clutter in the way is what you will be working around (PaintableFloor)

steps.do: Paint one stretch, walk back and look at it, then carry on.
steps.because: the texture you choose is stored separately from the surface, and it is what you pick that gets remembered (FloorTextureData)

steps.do: Treat a second coat as a proper repaint rather than a touch-up.
steps.because: the game keeps the previous floor as its own record, which is what a repaint replaces (OldFloorSaveData)

steps.do: Finish the floor before you restock for the day.
steps.because: the floor change is saved with the shop, so leaving it half done leaves the shop saved half done (FloorSaveData)

commonMistakes: Starting to paint with shelves and boxes still in the way.
Assuming a floor change is free or instant.
Repainting the whole shop on your busiest day instead of one section at a time.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
